overview.summary: Plumbers install, maintain and repair the pipes, fixtures and appliances that supply water and remove waste in homes and buildings.
overview.problems: They keep water supply, drainage and heating working safely and hygienically, and fix leaks and blockages.
overview.worksWith: Customers, builders, other tradespeople, suppliers and building inspectors.
overview.workplaces: Homes, offices, shops, factories and building sites, and many plumbers are self-employed.

timeline.title: Plan the jobs and load the van
timeline.description: The plumber checks the job list, customer details, parts and tools.
timeline.why: Arriving with the right parts avoids wasted trips.

timeline.title: Find the problem
timeline.description: The plumber asks the customer what happened, inspects pipes and fittings, and looks for the cause of a leak, blockage or low pressure.
timeline.why: Fixing the real cause prevents the problem coming back.

timeline.title: Repair or install
timeline.description: After shutting off the water, the plumber cuts and joins pipes and fits taps, toilets, boilers or drains.
timeline.why: Neat, correct joints prevent leaks and water damage.

timeline.title: Test and check
timeline.description: The plumber turns the water back on, tests for leaks, checks flow and drainage, and cleans up.
timeline.why: Testing proves the work is safe and sound.

timeline.title: Customer talk and paperwork
timeline.description: The plumber explains what was done, gives a price or invoice and advises how to avoid future problems.
timeline.why: Customers need to understand and trust the work.

timeline.title: Emergency call-outs
timeline.description: Burst pipes and blocked drains cannot wait, so plumbers are sometimes called out at short notice.
timeline.why: Water damage grows quickly if nothing is done.

responsibilities: Installing and repairing pipes, taps, toilets and heating systems
Finding the cause of leaks and blockages
Giving honest quotes and explaining the work
Keeping tools and the work area tidy and safe
Keeping records, and handling invoices if self-employed
challenges: The work is physically demanding, with kneeling, lifting and working in tight spaces.
Some jobs are dirty or unpleasant, such as blocked drains.
Emergency call-outs can come at any hour.
Work on gas or heating needs specific training and licences in many places.
Time and cost are hard to estimate when hidden problems appear.
Self-employed plumbers must find customers and manage money.
workEnvironment: Mostly on site in homes, commercial buildings and construction sites, often in tight, wet or dirty spaces. Many plumbers travel between jobs in a van. Some work for companies and others are self-employed, and hours can include emergency call-outs.
rewards: The satisfaction of fixing a problem
The option to run your own business
tradeoffs: Earnings and demand that vary by country, area and employer

activity.title: Map the water system in your home
steps: Walk around your home and note where water comes in, such as the main tap or meter, and where the taps, toilets and drains are.
Sketch a simple plan showing these points.
With an adult, find the main shut-off valve and learn how it turns off the water.
Look for any slow drips and tell an adult.
Note whether understanding how a system works felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You see how water supply and drainage are connected, which is the first step in diagnosing plumbing problems.
activity.safety: Do not repair pipes, touch gas or heating equipment or work under sinks with sharp tools. Ask a qualified plumber for any real repair.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
